task_instruction:
Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You are unable to send MMS messages using your messaging app for the past few hours. You want to fix it and successfully send an MMS message.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought:
I found the likely cause. Here's what I'm seeing on your account:

**Line 555-123-2002 (Line ID L1002) — Premium Plan**
- Status: **Active** (not suspended)
- Data used: **15.1 GB** of your **15.0 GB** plan limit
- Billing cycle ends: 2025-02-28

Your line has **exceeded its monthly data limit**, so data connectivity has been cut off. Since MMS (picture/video messaging) requires an active mobile data connection, messages will fail to send — which matches what you're experiencing.

To restore picture messaging, you can add more data to this line now. Your plan refuels at **$2.00 per GB**, and the maximum is **2 GB** (which would be **$4.00** for the full 2 GB).

How much data would you like to add — 1 GB ($2.00) or 2 GB ($4.00)?

turns.thought:
Thanks for those details. The key thing is that **Airplane Mode is ON** — that single setting disables the cellular radio, which is almost certainly why you're showing "no service," no signal, no network type, and why the phone is even reporting the SIM as missing. Mobile data is also switched off, and Wi‑Fi is off, so there's no data path at all right now (that's why MMS fails).

Let's work through this in order. Please do these one at a time and tell me what you see after each:

**Step 1 — Turn Airplane Mode OFF**
On your phone, open **Settings → Network & internet** (or **Connections** on some models) and switch **Airplane Mode** to **OFF**. Alternatively, swipe down from the top of the screen twice to open Quick Settings and tap the airplane icon so it's no longer highlighted.

**Step 2 — Re-check the status bar**
After about 30 seconds, look at the top of the screen. Do you now see signal bars and a network type (5G/4G/LTE)? Also check whether the SIM still reports "missing."

**Step 3 — If the SIM still shows "missing," reseat it**
Power the phone off, remove the SIM tray with the eject tool, take the SIM card out, wipe it gently with a dry cloth, reinsert it firmly, and put the tray back in. Then power the phone back on and check the status bar again.
*(Note: if instead the SIM reports "Locked" — asking for a PIN or PUK — stop there and tell me; that's something our technical support team has to handle.)*

**Step 4 — Turn Mobile Data ON**
Once you have signal, go to **Settings → Network & internet → Mobile network** (or **SIMs**) and switch **Mobile data** to **ON**. Also confirm **Data roaming** stays on, and you may want to switch **Wi‑Fi** on so you have a fallback data path.

**Step 5 — Send a test picture message**
Try sending an MMS again.

Just let me know what the status bar shows after Step 1 — that will tell us whether we need the SIM reseat at all. If you still have no service after reseating the SIM, I'll get you over to our technical support team, since that would point to a hardware or account-provisioning issue I can't fix from here.
turns.execution_output: User: Turning airplane mode off now.

turns.thought:
Yes — turn mobile data on now.

**Step 1 — Turn Mobile Data ON**
Go to **Settings → Network & internet → Mobile network** (or **SIMs**) and switch **Mobile data** to **ON**. Leave **Data roaming** on as it is.

**Step 2 — Fix the network mode (important for MMS)**
This is the bigger issue: you're on **2G**, and 2G generally isn't sufficient for picture/video messaging — MMS needs at least 3G. Please change your preferred network mode:
- Go to **Settings → Network & internet → Mobile network → Preferred network mode**
- Select **"5G/4G preferred"** (sometimes listed as "5G/LTE preferred" or similar)

This also explains the poor signal reading — the phone is holding onto an older, slower network.

**Step 3 — Give it a moment and re-check**
Wait about 30 seconds and look at the status bar. You should see the network type change from 2G to 4G/5G/LTE, and signal should improve. If it's still stuck on 2G, try toggling **Airplane Mode ON, wait 10 seconds, then OFF** to force the phone to reconnect to the network.

**Step 4 — Send a test picture message**
Once you're on 4G/5G with data enabled, try the MMS again.

Let me know what the status bar shows after Steps 1–3. If you're still stuck on 2G with no improvement, tell me and I'll get our technical support team involved, since that would point to a network coverage or provisioning issue I can't resolve from here.
turns.execution_output: User: Turning mobile data on first.

turns.thought:
Yes — go ahead and send that test picture message now. Your connection looks solid: SIM active, 5G, excellent signal, and mobile data on.

Try sending a picture to a friend (or even to your own number as a test). Let me know whether it goes through or fails.

- **If it sends successfully** — you're all set. The original problem was the data overage cutting off your data connection; that's resolved for this billing cycle, and your cycle resets on **2025-02-28**. Going forward, keep an eye on that 15 GB limit, since the same thing will happen again if you go over — you can refuel again, or we can look at a plan with more data if it keeps happening.
- **If it still fails** — please check these two things and tell me what you see:
  1. **APN settings** — Settings → Network & internet → Mobile network → Access point names. Check whether the MMSC URL is populated (it's the server address that handles picture messages).
  2. **Wi‑Fi Calling** — if Wi‑Fi Calling is ON, it can sometimes interfere with MMS.

If the MMSC URL is blank or Wi‑Fi Calling is on, we can correct both. Just report back and we'll take it from there.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check whether I can send an MMS.

turns.thought:
Both of those can block picture messaging, so let's fix them one at a time.

**Step 1 — Turn Wi‑Fi Calling OFF**
- Open **Settings → Network & internet → Calls & SMS** (or **Connections → Wi‑Fi Calling** on some phones)
- Switch **Wi‑Fi Calling** to **OFF**
- Leave Wi‑Fi itself off for now so we're testing purely over your 5G data connection

**Step 2 — Reset your APN settings**
Your APN name shows "internet," but the **MMSC URL is blank** — that's the server address that actually handles picture and video messages, so without it MMS can't go through.

- Go to **Settings → Network & internet → Mobile network → Access point names** (may be under **Advanced**)
- Tap the **⋮ menu** (three dots) in the top right
- Select **Reset to default**

**Step 3 — Reboot your phone**
This step is required — the new APN settings won't take effect until the phone restarts. Power the phone off and back on.

**Step 4 — Verify and test**
After the reboot:
- Confirm mobile data is still ON and you're still on 5G with signal
- Go back into **Access point names** and confirm the MMSC URL is now populated (it should show a server address instead of "Not Set")
- Confirm **Wi‑Fi Calling is OFF**
- Send your test picture message

Let me know what the MMSC URL shows after the reset and whether the picture message goes through. If the MMSC field is still blank after the reset and reboot — or if messages still fail — I'll get you over to our technical support team, since that would mean the settings aren't provisioning correctly on our end and I can't push them from here.
turns.execution_output: User: Turning Wi-Fi Calling off first.

turns.thought:
I understand the frustration — you've done all the right steps, and since your connection itself is healthy (5G, excellent signal, data on, MMSC populated, Wi‑Fi Calling off), we've ruled out the network‑side causes. That means we need to look at the messaging app itself rather than the connection.

Please check these two things on your phone:

**1. Messaging app permissions**
- Go to **Settings → Apps → Messages** (or your messaging app) → **Permissions**
- Look at whether **Storage** (sometimes called "Photos and videos" or "Files and media") and **SMS** are set to **Allowed**

The messaging app needs **Storage** to attach the picture and **SMS** to send it. If either is set to "Denied" or "Ask every time," MMS will fail even with a perfect connection. Please **allow both** if they aren't already.

**2. Data Saver / background data restrictions**
- Go to **Settings → Network & internet → Data Saver** and confirm **Data Saver is OFF**
- Then **Settings → Apps → Messages → Mobile data & Wi‑Fi** and confirm **Background data** is enabled and the app isn't marked as metered/restricted

Data Saver can starve the messaging app of the data it needs to upload a picture.

**3. VPN (if you use one)**
- If a VPN app is active, turn it **OFF** temporarily and retry

Please try sending a test picture message after making those changes and let me know the result.

If picture messages *still* fail after confirming the permissions and data restrictions, I'll transfer you to our technical support team — at that point the issue is on the account/provisioning side and needs tools I don't have access to from here. And to be clear about what we've already resolved: the 2 GB data refuel ($4.00) is applied and your line is healthy, so this is isolated to MMS specifically.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check the messaging app permissions and data restrictions.

turns.thought:
Yes — please grant the **SMS** permission to the messaging app. That's likely the missing piece: the app has Storage, so it can find your picture, but without SMS permission it can't actually hand the message off to be sent.

Please do this:
- Go to **Settings → Apps → Messages → Permissions**
- Look for **SMS** in the list. If it's there but set to "Denied," tap it and select **Allow**.
- If you don't see SMS listed at all, tap the **⋮ menu** (top right) and choose **All permissions** — sometimes it's collapsed and hidden there.

After granting it, **force-close the messaging app** (swipe it away from your recent apps) and reopen it, then send your test picture message.

Let me know whether it goes through. If SMS genuinely isn't available to grant on your phone, or if the message still fails after granting it, tell me and I'll get you transferred to our technical support team — we'll have exhausted everything I can do from this side.
turns.execution_output: User: Granting the SMS permission to the messaging app now.
